_comment: Input of tools/t0/r1g/suites_status.mjs: the console logs of tools/t0/run_suites.mjs runs on the R1g tree. Each log (and the summary JSON of the same run) is a byte-identical copy in docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/ (cmp, 2026-11-13) of the original under tmp/, which is git-ignored; 'time_utc' is the file time of the original when it was copied (a checkout has no file times, and the runs are ordered by it). Add a run by copying its log, adding an entry and regenerating. 'conditions' states only what a record shows and names that record; where it repeats a diagnosis, the sentence says whose diagnosis it is.

rows_added.why: the runner self-test (tools/t0/tests/runner_selftest.mjs) became a row on that day; older runs selected 79 suites

sources.conditions: Cloud container, 2026-11-04. 25 of the 79 suites then in the table have a row: the engineer stopped the run (docs/accept/R1G-STATUS.md 23:50: 'stopped by me'). By that record api.mapbox.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net were unreachable from the container then (curl http 000) and the engineer diagnosed the red map-dependent suites as that environment fault; this file states the diagnosis as theirs, not as a result. The original has a byte-identical twin, tmp/r1g-pack/suites-partial-networkblocked.log (cmp). Record: docs/accept/R1G-STATUS.md lines of 2026-11-04 21:15 and 23:50.

Cloud container, 2026-11-04, the R1-specific suites only (10 selected, every one has a row). By the record api.mapbox.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net were unreachable then. Record: docs/accept/R1G-STATUS.md line of 2026-11-04 23:50.

Cloud container, 2026-11-08, 8 suites selected, every one has a row. By the record api.mapbox.com answered 200 and cdn.jsdelivr.net 301 (curl) and T0_MAPBOX_UNREACHABLE was not set. Record: docs/accept/R1G-STATUS.md line of 2026-11-08.

Cloud container, file time 2026-11-09. A full run (79 selected) that stopped after 40 rows (its summary says PARTIAL). Not described in docs/accept/R1G-STATUS.md. The tail of its static.legal row names release/R1g/dist. No load was recorded.

Cloud container, file time 2026-11-11. A full run: 79 rows in the log (counted with grep and in the summary JSON, 79 distinct ids) and the runner's own final line '51/79 suites OK ... 13443s'. The task brief of 2026-11-13 gave '71 of 79 suites reached' for this log; the log and its summary have a row for every one of the 79 suites of the table as it was then, so that figure is not what the log shows. Node's proxy variables were not given to the suites: the four pagesfix rows ended in 0.4 to 0.6 s with every test failed on 'TypeError: fetch failed' in ensureVendor (their summary tails). The same brief says the run took place under heavy machine load; the log itself has no load. Not described in docs/accept/R1G-STATUS.md. The tails of its static.legal and r1.seo rows name release/R1g/dist.

Cloud container, file time 2026-11-11, written 80 minutes after the file time of the full run. A re-run of the 28 suites that were not OK in it (the selection file lists them, in the order of the full run) with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY set by hand in the shell (line 1 of the log is Node's EnvHttpProxyAgent warning of the runner process). It stopped after 14 of the 28 (4798 s of suites; its summary says PARTIAL). The log does not name the tree; the task brief of 2026-11-13 calls it the partial re-run of the R1g regression. No load was recorded.

Cloud container, 2026-11-13, one suite, through the machine lock, with the first proxy-aware runner (no manual environment: the runner added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY itself) and a cold vendor cache (T0_AGENT=r1g-harness-after), so the suite had to fetch the Mapbox GL library with Node. Load recorded in the log (5.17 at the start and at the end, 4 CPUs).

Cloud container, 2026-11-13, the 16 static rows (--only static), through the machine lock, with the first proxy-aware runner (it added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY where unset; no NODE_OPTIONS flag yet). Load recorded (5.17 at the start of the run, 6.77 at its end, 4 CPUs, shared with other work: the durations are not timing evidence). static.baseline is 16/17 in this run: case 16 of tools/t0/tests/baseline_selftest.py parses the last line of a Node child's merged output and the child had printed Node's two-line proxy warning (red-first proof and fix: docs/accept/R1G-STATUS.md, 2026-11-13 line; docs/accept/README.md, 'Behind a proxy').

Cloud container, 2026-11-13, six static rows (--only static.baseline,static.legal,static.overlap.selftest,static.ship: the suite that regressed in the run before, and the light rows), started directly (not through the machine lock: each is a few seconds of CPU) with the final proxy-aware runner and no manual environment: the console line of the run says it added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY and extended NODE_OPTIONS. Load recorded in the log (10.08 at the start, 11.15 at the end, 4 CPUs, shared with other work: the durations are not timing evidence). static.baseline is 17/17 here.

Cloud container, 2026-11-13, the 16 static rows (--only static), through the machine lock, with the final proxy-aware runner and no manual environment (its summary says the children's environment got: added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY; extended NODE_OPTIONS). Load recorded: 12.47 at the start and 12.49 at the end of the run, 4 CPUs, shared with other work: the durations are not timing evidence. The run reached its final line. This entry was written by a script (tmp/r1g-harness2/post-add-sources.mjs) when the queued job ended; it makes no diagnosis.

Cloud container, 2026-11-13, six rows from other groups (--only pagesfix.R1c.legal,pagesmaps.R1a,r1.seo,r1.acc,staging.R0,a11y.R1a.chooser), through the machine lock, with the final proxy-aware runner and no manual environment (its summary says the children's environment got: added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY; extended NODE_OPTIONS). Load recorded: 12.49 at the start and 11.44 at the end of the run, 4 CPUs, shared with other work: the durations are not timing evidence. The run reached its final line. This entry was written by a script (tmp/r1g-harness2/post-add-sources.mjs) when the queued job ended; it makes no diagnosis.

Cloud container, 2026-11-13, the two rows static.runner and static.hygiene (--only static.runner,static.hygiene) after the review fix of the load fields of the commands of checks 1 and 8 of tools/accept (the self-test file of this run has 21 tests, the earlier logs of the day show 19; one is skipped: the opt-in online test), through the machine lock, with the final proxy-aware runner and no manual environment (its summary says the children's environment got: added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY; extended NODE_OPTIONS). Load recorded: 12.67 at the start and 11.33 at the end of the run, 4 CPUs, shared with other work: the durations are not timing evidence. The run reached its final line. This entry was written by a script (tmp/r1g-harness2/post-add-sources.mjs) when the queued job ended; it makes no diagnosis.

Cloud container, 2026-11-13, a verification run of the final proxy-aware runner (one suite, which downloads the pinned Mapbox GL library with its own Node fetch() code (tests/t0/pages-maps.spec.mjs)): `node tools/t0/run_suites.mjs --r1-dist release/R1g/dist --no-red --no-network --only pagesmaps.R1a --port-base 19040` (1 rows: pagesmaps.R1a; a prefix in --only can select more than one suite), started by the run script tmp/r1g-verify2/e2e-inner.sh inside one slot of the machine lock, with no manual environment: by its header the shell had HTTPS_PROXY set and NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY unset (its summary says the children's environment got: added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY; extended NODE_OPTIONS). Header written by the run script: maps start 2026-11-14T00:04:03Z load1 13.24; HTTPS_PROXY set: yes; NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=<unset>; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt; NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca; T0_MAPBOX_UNREACHABLE=<unset>; vendor caches before: ls: cannot access 'tmp/r1g-verify2-maps/vendor': No such file or directory ls: cannot access 'tmp/t0-maps/vendor': No such file or directory  / maps end 2026-11-14T00:04:06Z load1 13.62; runner exit 1; vendor cache after: mapbox-gl.css mapbox-gl.js. Runner exit code 1. Rows: pagesmaps.R1a FAIL 1/1. Load recorded: 13.24 at the start and 13.62 at the end of the run, 4 CPUs, shared with other work: the durations are not timing evidence (measured on the cloud machine (4 vCPU container, software GL)). The run reached its final line. This entry was written by tmp/r1g-verify2/register.mjs from the summary JSON, the header file, the exit-code file and the run script; it made no diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS ADDED 2026-11-14 by the release-r1g engineer (a diagnosis, not a fact that run recorded: its header does not list T0_CHROME). The summary tail of the row (three lines: '  ]', '}', 'Node.js v22.23.4') and the row itself (1 PASS line, then the process ended with exit 1 after 2.5 s) are what an unhandled Node error that ends a suite after its first test looks like. The vendor cache after the run held mapbox-gl.css and mapbox-gl.js, so the download through the proxy that the runner enables had worked. Reproduced the same day on the same tree, without a browser starting: with the harness environment added by hand (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1, NODE_OPTIONS='--use-openssl-ca --disable-warning=UNDICI-EHPA', as child_env.mjs gives it), a cold vendor cache and T0_CHROME UNSET, `node tests/t0/pages-maps.spec.mjs --dist release/R1g/dist --filter 'PG-01|PG-02-camera'` printed PG-01 PASS and then died with 'Error: spawn C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe ENOENT' (tests/t0/lib.mjs: CHROME = T0_CHROME or the Windows path; the spawn has no 'error' handler), its last three lines being '  ]', '}', 'Node.js v22.23.4', exit 1, 6.5 s wall (log docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/2026-11-14-pagesmaps-no-chrome-repro.log). The same row through the real runner, with no browser started (T0_CHROME unset, a cold vendor cache, `node tools/t0/run_suites.mjs --r1-dist release/R1g/dist --no-red --no-network --only pagesmaps.R1a --port-base 19340`, runner exit 1, 1.4 s, load 6.89>6.89, 4 CPUs, measured on the cloud machine (4 vCPU container, software GL)): `FAIL pagesmaps.R1a 1/1`, the summary tail '  ]', '}', 'Node.js v22.23.4', and both vendor files in the cache afterwards, that is the row of the 00:04 run again (logs docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/2026-11-14-pagesmaps-runner-no-chrome-repro.log and .summary.json). Control, same suite in the shell as the container gives it (HTTPS_PROXY set, NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY unset, T0_CHROME set, cold cache): PG-02-camera FAIL 'TypeError: fetch failed' in ensureVendor and no vendor file written (log docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/2026-11-14-pagesmaps-no-proxy-env-control.log), which is the failure that the summary tails of the pagesfix rows of the full run of 2026-11-11 show ('TypeError: fetch failed' in ensureVendor; the tails of the pagesmaps rows of that run do not name the cause, but the 20 tests that failed in them are the ones that call ensureVendor) and what the proxy rule removes. The repeat of this run with T0_CHROME set was queued behind the machine lock when this diagnosis was written (tmp/r1g-final/e2e-inner.sh); when it has run, its entry is the one whose log is docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/2026-11-14-pagesmaps-cold-cache-chrome-set.log.
